tool.name: PyEuk cluster (current)
tool.description: wIBS distance + cluster SWEEP + graphical report, PyEuk v0.7.0
tool.command: mkdir -p wrk && export TMPDIR="\$(pwd)/wrk" && python '$__tool_directory__/pyeuk_cluster.py' --sheet '$sheet' --matrix-out '$distance_matrix' --clusters-out '$clusters' --sweep-out '$sweep' --report-out '$report' --n-boot $advanced.n_boot --linkage-method $advanced.linkage_method --report-flavor $advanced.report_flavor --report-theme $advanced.report_theme --min-completeness $advanced.min_completeness --k-min $advanced.k_min --k-max $advanced.k_max --report-excluded $advanced.report_excluded --project-psd $advanced.project_psd --cut $advanced.cut #if str($advanced.linkage_threshold).strip() != '' --linkage-threshold $advanced.linkage_threshold #end if

param.name: project_psd
param.label: Project distances onto the PSD cone
param.help: OFF by default. The projection makes the distances embed in Euclidean space, which Ward assumes, but it compresses the closest pairs -- on one cohort it left the median pair almost unchanged while inflating the closest 1% by a factor of 19.6. Tight pairs are what a relatedness measure exists to resolve. Off improved pairwise AUC on all four labelled comparisons: Cyclospora went from 3 errors in 153 to 1, PvAmpSeq from 5 in 277 to 2. Turn it ON together with a distance cut, where the regularised geometry helps instead.

param.name: cut
param.label: How to cut the tree
param.help: Choose a cluster COUNT for a closed investigation where every specimen belongs somewhere. Cut at a DISTANCE for surveillance, where most specimens are unrelated and the true structure is mostly singletons -- a cluster count cannot represent that shape.

param.name: linkage_threshold
param.label: Distance to cut at
param.help: Distance-cut mode only. Leave empty to calibrate it from the data and print where the value came from.

param.name: n_boot
param.label: Bootstrap resamples (sweep confidence)
param.help: More resamples = steadier support estimates; 200 is the package default.

param.name: linkage_method
param.label: Linkage method
param.help: ward (default) makes compact blobs. single follows chains (transmission-like) but chains through noise.

param.name: report_theme
param.label: Report theme
param.help: galaxy = system fonts + Galaxy palette, no external assets (renders inline in Galaxy). studio = Fraunces/Inter via Google Fonts (standalone viewing).

tool.help:
Identical driver to the Cyclospora arm's PyEuk tool, but resolving against a SEPARATE image pinned to PyEuk **v0.7.0** (tag ``v0.7.0``, commit ``cf07dc88``) rather than to commit d8e45a81.
That pin is deliberate and must not be merged with the Cyclospora arm's. The arm's reference result (label-free k=2, ARI 0.9721) was measured against d8e45a81 and moving it would invalidate a published number. This workflow needs two fixes that landed after it:
* ``37f59a3`` — unobserved allele columns no longer inflate the wIBS denominator (spond/pyeuk#8). Without it distances are compressed roughly fivefold. * ``1f61e15`` — ``weight_mode`` is now selectable and defaults to **heterozygosity** ``2p(1-p)``. The old KING form ``1/sqrt(p(1-p))`` is inverted for presence/absence input: it weights RARE alleles hardest, while all the discriminating signal sits in balanced columns. Measured consequence on a Cyclospora sheet: a near-universal column at p=0.9456 drew weight 4.4 against 2.0 for a perfectly informative one, and its inclusion moved ARI from 0.9212 to 0.7536. Under heterozygosity the same column weighs 0.10. * ``13b808d`` — the minimum-cluster-size guard became ``max(2, min(5, int(0.10*n)))``. The old ``max(5, ...)`` made k>1 structurally unreachable for any cohort of n<=9, and for n=10 accepted only an exact 5/5 split. A 10-specimen, 3-species cohort collapsed to k=1 purely on that integer comparison, despite a clean 7/3 knee at 4.5x the noise floor.
